findings.scenario: Bundle validation only requires each fragment hash to appear once in its authority-class list and once in orderedMaterializationHashes. The same fragment set can therefore validate under many permutations, including untrusted-data before policy/human/skill layers. Prose says the closed context policy uniquely determines order/roles, but that predicate is not checked, so materialization is not deterministic and quoted prior-output can be packed first.
findings.remediation: Fail validation unless orderedMaterializationHashes equals the unique sequence produced by contextPolicyHash over the authority-class lists (closed layer order and closed intra-layer sort). Any other permutation is invalid.

findings.scenario: HumanInterruptV1 is a closed immutable hash record with no decision slot or stateRevision, and the interrupted segment is not required to bind exactly one interruptHash. Two schema-valid HumanDecisionV1 rows can share an interruptHash (accept vs reject), and a second interrupt row for the same (jobId, segmentId) can be decided independently. The claimed undecided→decided CAS has no record to apply to without mutating interruptHash.
findings.remediation: Keep HumanInterruptV1 immutable. Add a control-plane InterruptDecisionSlotV1 CAS (undecided→decided, one decisionHash). The active→interrupted CAS must store that unique interruptHash as the only resume/terminal authority; other interrupt or decision hashes cannot resume or terminal the segment.

findings.line: active→interrupted attempt settlement (~398-401) vs accept-proposal resume (~441-444)
findings.scenario: Interrupt must stop work and settle any in-flight attempt to a non-ambiguous attempt state, while accept-proposal resumes the same segment and creates no new attempt. Non-ambiguous attempt states are terminal (completed/failed/cancelled/ambiguous) and cannot be revived. If the attempt is cancelled to stop work, resume is stuck active with no attempt; if it stays in-flight, the interrupt did not stop work; if it is completed then rejected, a completed attempt coexists with a cancelled segment that must not carry a proposal.
findings.remediation: Close the attempt/segment pair: interrupt is legal only when the attempt is already schema-valid completed with an unapplied proposal (segment interrupted, no apply) or the in-flight attempt CASes to cancelled/ambiguous and accept-proposal is illegal. accept-proposal may CAS interrupted→active only in the completed-attempt case and then terminalize the same attempt; reject/expiry CASes the segment to cancelled with no proposalEnvelopeHash.

findings.scenario: Reserved product commands cannot be aliased, but commandName is not required to be absent from the reserved-name policy. Registering commandName help/cancel/release (or another reserved token) yields a skill-bound SlashCommandEntryV1 whose primary name is the product command; parse then invokes the skill instead of the reserved control.
findings.remediation: Registration and parse fail closed if commandName or any alias is in the reserved-name policy under the same case-folding rule as collisions. Reserved names cannot be skill command names.

findings.scenario: Apply eligibility requires a completed RouteSegmentReceiptV1 whose foundationJobReceiptHash is the frozen owner named by the receipt-bundle manifest, but RouteSegmentReceiptV1 has no foundationJobReceiptHash. Implementers who follow the field list skip the frozen-owner check and treat a completed adjacent segment receipt plus envelope as apply-eligible, creating a second apply authority.
findings.remediation: Require a schema-valid ReceiptBundleManifestV1 for that jobId whose routeSegmentReceiptHashes contains this completed segment receipt hash and whose foundationJobReceiptHash is the unique frozen-contract terminal job receipt. Do not add foundationJobReceiptHash to RouteSegmentReceiptV1.

findings.scenario: Fragment freshness is checked at pack time, but after reservation invocation and resume only require contextBundleHash to equal the frozen segment hash. A bundle past expiresAt, or a fragment whose freshness/rights later fail, still invokes because the hash matches. That is fail-open on context lifetime.
findings.remediation: Invocation, dispatch, and resume fail closed when now >= bundle.expiresAt or any included fragment freshness/rights/expiry fails. Frozen contextBundleHash is identity, not a waiver of live expiry.

findings.scenario: Unowned/expired/revoked skills cannot parse or invoke, and kill switches reject before grammar, but invocation equality only checks reserved hashes and SkillSet membership. A disabled skill admission hash (or enabled command bound to a disabled/fixture-mismatched skill) still creates a SkillInvocationIntentV1 after reservation. Disabled is not a live fail-closed gate.
findings.remediation: Parse and intent creation fail closed unless current command and bound skill admission are fixture-only (or a later authorized enabled), unkilled, unexpired, and owned. Hash membership in the reserved SkillSetV1 does not override live admission.

audit.proof_assessment: The supplied Grok findings JSON describes a pre-remediation draft (no interrupted CAS, no command killSwitchRef, no sourceKind map, no invocation-manifest equality). Current bytes remediate those HIGH items in prose and now match Step 2's interrupted state, but they are still a planning contract with no executable oracle. Treat that JSON as stale evidence of prior holes, not as a CLEAN certificate of these bytes. Remaining defects are unclosed predicates on materialization uniqueness, interrupt CAS identity, reserved commandName, apply's frozen-owner lookup, and live expiry/admission.
residual_risks: ContextFragmentV1.normalizedBytes is unnamed as a count vs payload; embedding bytes would put content into hash-chained control records.
excludedFragmentReceipts[] has no closed reason vocabulary, so size drops of untrusted fragments can be labeled non-overflow.
HumanInterruptV1.issuer is a spoofable literal; issuerPolicyHash does not by itself prove control-plane authorship.
effectiveToolGrantHash as a recorded subset cannot be proven from hashes alone unless both grant bodies are resolved and intersected.
safeSummary derived from typed proposal fields remains a social-engineering channel.
Composer bidi/homoglyph display can spoof slash names while ASCII parse stays closed; newline class is not enumerated beyond 'newline'.
Mandatory human-decision fragments can deadlock first-turn packing if 'applicable route' is read as always-required.
SkillInvocationReceiptV1 terminal states are not a closed enum with the same non-completed proposal ban.
No accessibility contract for pre-dispatch included/excluded source disclosure.
Future child receipts can cycle if parent/child hashing is not creation-ordered; first slice has zero children.
